question: Count total registered customers.
aggregation_semantics: Scalar COUNT(*) aggregation of registered customers
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_customers FROM customers WHERE account_status = 'active';

question: Find the top 20 products by total sales revenue.
aggregation_semantics: SUM(order_items.line_total) grouped by product, ordered descending limit 20
reference_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.title, ROUND(SUM(oi.line_total), 2) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Calculate monthly gross merchandise value for the last year of orders.
aggregation_semantics: Monthly SUM(total_amount) grouped by strftime('%Y-%m', order_date)
reference_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS order_month, ROUND(SUM(total_amount), 2) AS gross_merchandise_value, COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders FROM orders WHERE order_status IN ('completed', 'returned') GROUP BY order_month ORDER BY order_month;

question: Find the top sellers by net revenue after deducting commissions and refunds.
aggregation_semantics: Net seller payout aggregation after marketplace commission deduction
reference_sql: SELECT s.seller_id, s.seller_name, ROUND(SUM(sp.gross_sales), 2) AS total_gross_sales, ROUND(SUM(sp.commission_deducted), 2) AS total_commissions, ROUND(SUM(sp.net_payout), 2) AS net_seller_payout FROM sellers s JOIN seller_payouts sp ON s.seller_id = sp.seller_id WHERE sp.payout_status = 'completed' GROUP BY s.seller_id, s.seller_name ORDER BY net_seller_payout DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Calculate average order value by customer segment.
aggregation_semantics: AVG(orders.total_amount) grouped by segment name
reference_sql: SELECT cs.segment_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders, ROUND(AVG(o.total_amount), 2) AS average_order_value FROM customer_segments cs JOIN customer_segment_memberships csm ON cs.segment_id = csm.segment_id JOIN orders o ON csm.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY cs.segment_name ORDER BY average_order_value DESC;

question: Find products with high ratings (average >= 4.5) and low sales volume (less than 10 units).
aggregation_semantics: HAVING filter on AVG(rating) >= 4.5 and COALESCE(SUM(quantity), 0) < 10
reference_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.title, ROUND(AVG(pr.rating), 2) AS avg_rating, COUNT(DISTINCT pr.review_id) AS review_count, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS total_units_sold FROM products p JOIN product_reviews pr ON p.product_id = pr.product_id LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title HAVING avg_rating >= 4.5 AND total_units_sold < 10 ORDER BY avg_rating DESC, total_units_sold ASC LIMIT 20;

question: Identify customers with multiple returned orders.
aggregation_semantics: COUNT(return_id) grouped by customer, filtered with HAVING return_count > 1
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, c.email, COUNT(r.return_id) AS returned_order_count FROM customers c JOIN returns r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, c.email HAVING returned_order_count > 1 ORDER BY returned_order_count DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Calculate the percentage of orders delivered late according to carrier estimates.
aggregation_semantics: Conditional percentage: (COUNT(delivered_at > estimated_delivery) / COUNT(*)) * 100
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_shipments, SUM(CASE WHEN delivered_at > estimated_delivery THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_shipments, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivered_at > estimated_delivery THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_delivery_percentage FROM shipments WHERE shipment_status = 'delivered' AND delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND estimated_delivery IS NOT NULL;

question: Find abandoned shopping carts containing valuable products.
aggregation_semantics: SUM(products.base_price * cart_items.quantity) for abandoned carts
reference_sql: SELECT c.cart_id, cu.customer_id, cu.email, COUNT(ci.cart_item_id) AS items_in_cart, ROUND(SUM(p.base_price * ci.quantity), 2) AS estimated_cart_value FROM carts c JOIN customers cu ON c.customer_id = cu.customer_id JOIN cart_items ci ON c.cart_id = ci.cart_id JOIN products p ON ci.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.status = 'abandoned' GROUP BY c.cart_id, cu.customer_id, cu.email HAVING estimated_cart_value > 100.00 ORDER BY estimated_cart_value DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Compare marketplace seller performance across product categories.
aggregation_semantics: Total sales volume and revenue per category breakdown
reference_sql: SELECT cat.category_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.seller_id) AS active_sellers, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS items_sold, ROUND(SUM(oi.line_total), 2) AS category_revenue FROM categories cat JOIN products p ON cat.category_id = p.category_id JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY cat.category_name ORDER BY category_revenue DESC;

question: Calculate inventory turnover and reserved stock ratio across warehouses.
aggregation_semantics: SUM(stock_quantity), SUM(reserved_quantity), and reserved percentage per warehouse
reference_sql: SELECT w.warehouse_code, w.warehouse_name, SUM(i.stock_quantity) AS total_on_hand, SUM(i.reserved_quantity) AS total_reserved, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(i.reserved_quantity) / NULLIF(SUM(i.stock_quantity), 0), 2) AS reservation_rate_pct FROM warehouses w JOIN inventory i ON w.warehouse_id = i.warehouse_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_code, w.warehouse_name ORDER BY total_on_hand DESC;

question: Find products with stock shortages (on hand below reorder point) and recent order demand.
aggregation_semantics: Inventory on hand < reorder_point joined with sum of units ordered
reference_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.title, SUM(i.stock_quantity) AS current_stock, MIN(i.reorder_point) AS reorder_threshold, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p JOIN inventory i ON p.product_id = i.product_id JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title HAVING current_stock < reorder_threshold AND units_sold > 0 ORDER BY current_stock ASC LIMIT 20;

question: Calculate coupon redemption rates and total discounts surrendered.
aggregation_semantics: COUNT(redemption_id) and SUM(discount_applied) per coupon code
reference_sql: SELECT c.code, c.discount_type, c.discount_val, COUNT(cr.redemption_id) AS total_redemptions, ROUND(SUM(cr.discount_applied), 2) AS total_discount_granted FROM coupons c LEFT JOIN coupon_redemptions cr ON c.coupon_id = cr.coupon_id GROUP BY c.code, c.discount_type, c.discount_val ORDER BY total_redemptions DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Analyze conversion rates and cost per click by marketing campaign.
aggregation_semantics: Click-through rate (clicks / impressions) and total click spend per campaign
reference_sql: SELECT c.campaign_name, c.channel, COUNT(DISTINCT ai.impression_id) AS impressions, COUNT(DISTINCT ac.click_id) AS clicks, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT ac.click_id) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT ai.impression_id), 0), 2) AS click_through_rate_pct, ROUND(SUM(ac.cost_per_click), 2) AS total_click_spend FROM campaigns c LEFT JOIN ad_impressions ai ON c.campaign_id = ai.campaign_id LEFT JOIN ad_clicks ac ON c.campaign_id = ac.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_name, c.channel ORDER BY impressions DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Compare campaign advertising spend with attributed product revenue.
aggregation_semantics: Campaign spend vs attributed product revenue with ROI calculation
reference_sql: SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, c.spend AS advertising_spend, ROUND(SUM(oi.line_total), 2) AS product_gross_revenue, ROUND((SUM(oi.line_total) - c.spend) / NULLIF(c.spend, 0), 2) AS estimated_roas FROM campaigns c JOIN ad_impressions ai ON c.campaign_id = ai.campaign_id JOIN order_items oi ON ai.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, c.spend ORDER BY estimated_roas DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Find customers with repeated failed payment attempts.
aggregation_semantics: COUNT(payment_id) where status = 'failed' grouped by customer
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.email, COUNT(p.payment_id) AS failed_payment_attempts, ROUND(SUM(p.amount), 2) AS attempted_failed_volume FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN payments p ON o.order_id = p.order_id WHERE p.payment_status = 'failed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.email HAVING failed_payment_attempts >= 1 ORDER BY failed_payment_attempts DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Analyze return volumes and refund amounts by product category.
aggregation_semantics: COUNT(return_item_id) and SUM(refund_item_amount) grouped by category
reference_sql: SELECT cat.category_name, COUNT(ri.return_item_id) AS returned_items_count, ROUND(SUM(ri.refund_item_amount), 2) AS total_refunded_amount FROM categories cat JOIN products p ON cat.category_id = p.category_id JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN return_items ri ON oi.order_item_id = ri.order_item_id GROUP BY cat.category_name ORDER BY total_refunded_amount DESC;

question: Compare average shipping costs and delivery duration across logistics carriers.
aggregation_semantics: AVG(shipping_cost) and shipment count per carrier
reference_sql: SELECT sc.carrier_name, sc.service_tier, COUNT(s.shipment_id) AS total_packages_shipped, ROUND(AVG(s.shipping_cost), 2) AS average_shipping_cost, ROUND(SUM(s.shipping_cost), 2) AS total_carrier_spend FROM shipping_carriers sc JOIN shipments s ON sc.carrier_id = s.carrier_id GROUP BY sc.carrier_name, sc.service_tier ORDER BY total_packages_shipped DESC;

question: Calculate customer repeat-purchase rates.
aggregation_semantics: Proportion of customers with count(order_id) >= 2
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS total_ordering_customers, SUM(CASE WHEN order_count >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS repeat_buyers, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_count >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id), 2) AS repeat_buyer_percentage FROM (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(order_id) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'completed' GROUP BY customer_id);

question: Analyze recurring subscription statuses and monthly recurring revenue (MRR).
aggregation_semantics: SUM(price_per_cycle) grouped by subscription status
reference_sql: SELECT status, COUNT(subscription_id) AS subscriber_count, ROUND(SUM(price_per_cycle), 2) AS total_monthly_run_rate FROM subscriptions GROUP BY status ORDER BY subscriber_count DESC;

question: Analyze customer support ticket resolution times by problem category.
aggregation_semantics: AVG(resolution_time_hours) and COUNT(ticket_id) grouped by category
reference_sql: SELECT category, priority, COUNT(ticket_id) AS ticket_volume, ROUND(AVG(resolution_time_hours), 2) AS avg_resolution_hours, MIN(resolution_time_hours) AS fastest_resolution, MAX(resolution_time_hours) AS slowest_resolution FROM support_tickets WHERE status = 'resolved' GROUP BY category, priority ORDER BY avg_resolution_hours DESC;

question: Calculate marketplace seller commission deductions and net payout obligations.
aggregation_semantics: Monthly SUM(gross_sales), SUM(commission_deducted), and SUM(net_payout)
reference_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', payout_date) AS payout_month, COUNT(payout_id) AS total_disbursements, ROUND(SUM(gross_sales), 2) AS aggregate_gross_sales, ROUND(SUM(commission_deducted), 2) AS total_platform_commission, ROUND(SUM(net_payout), 2) AS total_seller_disbursed FROM seller_payouts WHERE payout_status = 'completed' GROUP BY payout_month ORDER BY payout_month;

question: Identify orders with high refund-to-order ratio.
aggregation_semantics: SUM(refund_amount) / total_amount per order
reference_sql: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_number, o.total_amount, ROUND(SUM(r.refund_amount), 2) AS refunded_sum, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(r.refund_amount) / o.total_amount, 2) AS refund_ratio_pct FROM orders o JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE r.refund_status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.order_number, o.total_amount HAVING refund_ratio_pct >= 90.0 ORDER BY refunded_sum DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Calculate daily orders and net revenue trends from daily sales metrics.
aggregation_semantics: Ordering of daily sales metrics with 7-day rolling aggregates
reference_sql: SELECT metric_date, total_orders, gross_merchandise_value, total_refunds, net_sales, new_customers_count FROM daily_sales_metrics ORDER BY metric_date DESC LIMIT 30;

question: Find top-selling product variants by revenue contribution.
aggregation_semantics: SUM(order_items.line_total) grouped by variant
reference_sql: SELECT p.title AS product_name, pv.variant_name, pv.variant_sku, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS order_occurrences, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold, ROUND(SUM(oi.line_total), 2) AS variant_revenue FROM product_variants pv JOIN products p ON pv.product_id = p.product_id JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.title, pv.variant_name, pv.variant_sku ORDER BY variant_revenue DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Compare warehouse storage utilization against capacity.
aggregation_semantics: SUM(stock_quantity) / capacity_units per warehouse
reference_sql: SELECT w.warehouse_code, w.warehouse_name, w.capacity_units, SUM(i.stock_quantity) AS current_inventory, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(i.stock_quantity) / w.capacity_units, 2) AS capacity_utilization_pct FROM warehouses w JOIN inventory i ON w.warehouse_id = i.warehouse_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_code, w.warehouse_name, w.capacity_units ORDER BY capacity_utilization_pct DESC;

question: Identify brands with the highest customer review ratings (minimum 50 reviews).
aggregation_semantics: AVG(rating) grouped by brand having count >= 50
reference_sql: SELECT b.brand_name, b.country_of_origin, COUNT(pr.review_id) AS total_reviews, ROUND(AVG(pr.rating), 2) AS average_rating FROM brands b JOIN products p ON b.brand_id = p.brand_id JOIN product_reviews pr ON p.product_id = pr.product_id GROUP BY b.brand_name, b.country_of_origin HAVING total_reviews >= 50 ORDER BY average_rating DESC, total_reviews DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Analyze order status transitions and fulfillment completion rate.
aggregation_semantics: Order count and percentage grouped by order_status
reference_sql: SELECT order_status, COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(order_id) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders), 2) AS status_percentage FROM orders GROUP BY order_status ORDER BY total_orders DESC;

question: Calculate customer lifetime value (CLV) defined as total completed spend minus refunds.
aggregation_semantics: SUM(orders.total_amount) - COALESCE(SUM(refunds.refund_amount), 0) per customer
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, c.email, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS completed_orders, ROUND(SUM(DISTINCT o.total_amount), 2) AS gross_spend, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_amount), 0), 2) AS total_refunded, ROUND(SUM(DISTINCT o.total_amount) - COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_amount), 0), 2) AS customer_lifetime_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, c.email ORDER BY customer_lifetime_value DESC LIMIT 20;

question: Execute multi-domain reconciliation combining customers, orders, order items, products, sellers, payments, and returns.
aggregation_semantics: Full relational join joining 7 core tables across customer, order, marketplace, and return domains
reference_sql: SELECT o.order_number, c.email AS customer_email, p.title AS product_title, s.seller_name, oi.quantity, oi.unit_price, oi.line_total, pay.payment_status, ret.return_reason FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN sellers s ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id JOIN payments pay ON o.order_id = pay.order_id LEFT JOIN returns ret ON o.order_id = ret.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'completed' LIMIT 20;

question: Cross-Database: Compare monthly ecommerce order revenue with corporate finance ledger recognized revenue.
aggregation_semantics: Subqueries independently executed on ecommerce and finance connections, joined in memory on month key
reference_sql: -- Subquery 1 (ecommerce): SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, ROUND(SUM(total_amount), 2) AS gmv FROM orders GROUP BY month; -- Subquery 2 (finance): SELECT fiscal_month AS month, recognized_revenue FROM ledger_monthly_revenue;

question: Cross-Database: Reconcile external marketing campaign expenditure with internal product sales revenue.
aggregation_semantics: Subqueries independently executed on marketing and ecommerce connections, joined on campaign_id
reference_sql: -- Subquery 1 (marketing): SELECT campaign_id, spend FROM external_campaigns; -- Subquery 2 (ecommerce): SELECT campaign_id, ROUND(SUM(line_total), 2) AS attributed_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN ad_impressions ai ON oi.product_id = ai.product_id GROUP BY campaign_id;
